title: "Add-on helpers — frozen model and standardized comparisons"
output: html_notebook

Functions used only by the additional research notebooks. These functions never
refit or overwrite an existing classifier.

## Locate the frozen study run

The model and predictions come from the current numbered run when the master
workflow is used. Standalone execution can still read a previously completed
source run.

```{r source-run-helpers}
get_source_run_id <- function() {
    source_id <- Sys.getenv("ATG_SOURCE_RUN_ID", unset = "")
    if (!grepl("^[0-9]{4,}$", source_id)) {
        stop("Run notebooks/14_Run_Additional_Insights.Rmd first")
    }
    source_id
}

source_run_path <- function(area, stem, extension = "rds") {
    if (!area %in% c("models", "checkpoints", "tables")) {
        stop("Unsupported original-run output folder: ", area)
    }
    source_id <- get_source_run_id()
    path <- file.path(
        project_root,
        "outputs",
        paste0("run_", source_id),
        area,
        sprintf("%s_run_%s.%s", stem, source_id, extension)
    )
    if (!file.exists(path)) {
        stop("Source run artifact does not exist: ", path)
    }
    path
}

load_source_rds <- function(area, stem) {
    readRDS(source_run_path(area, stem))
}

load_source_table <- function(stem) {
    data.table::fread(source_run_path("tables", stem, "csv"))
}

get_source_model <- function() {
    selected <- load_source_rds("models", "05_frozen_selection")
    if (!selected$chosen_family %in% c("logistic", "lasso", "forest")) {
        stop("Unexpected selected model family")
    }
    list(
        selection = selected,
        fitted = load_source_rds("models", paste0("05_", selected$chosen_family))
    )
}
```

## Weighted standardization and comparison

Creates an equal-mixture target distribution for AI/AN-alone and other
single-race respondents. The standardized weights are not original BRFSS
probability weights and do not make the comparison causal.

```{r composition-helpers}
# Returns only cells with at least min_cell_n respondents from BOTH groups.
# The same eligible cells can be reused in bootstrap replicates.
find_common_cells <- function(data, cell_column, min_cell_n = 30L) {
    counts <- data[cohort %in% primary_groups, .N, by = c("cohort", cell_column)]
    cell_name <- as.character(counts[[cell_column]])
    ai_cells <- cell_name[
        counts$cohort == primary_groups[1] & counts$N >= min_cell_n
    ]
    other_cells <- cell_name[
        counts$cohort == primary_groups[2] & counts$N >= min_cell_n
    ]
    intersect(ai_cells, other_cells)
}

# Recomputes the group-standardization factors from the supplied weights.
# These factors make each group share the same age/sex target distribution.
standardize_weights <- function(data, raw_weights, cell_column, common_cells) {
    if (length(raw_weights) != nrow(data)) {
        stop("Standardization weight vector length mismatch")
    }
    selected <- data.table::copy(data)
    selected[, base_weight := as.numeric(raw_weights)]
    selected <- selected[
        cohort %in% primary_groups &
            get(cell_column) %in% common_cells &
            valid_weight(base_weight)
    ]
    if (nrow(selected) == 0L) {
        stop("Standardization has no positive-weight observations")
    }
    distribution <- selected[, .(
        total_weight = sum(base_weight)
    ), by = c("cohort", cell_column)]
    distribution[, share := total_weight / sum(total_weight), by = cohort]

    # A common cell must retain positive weight in each replicate and group.
    present <- distribution[, .N, by = cell_column]
    if (any(present$N != 2L) || nrow(present) != length(common_cells)) {
        stop("Bootstrap lost positivity in a standardization cell")
    }

    target <- distribution[, .(
        target_share = mean(share)
    ), by = cell_column]
    distribution <- merge(
        distribution,
        target,
        by = cell_column,
        sort = FALSE
    )
    distribution[, adjustment := target_share / share]
    if (any(!is.finite(distribution$adjustment))) {
        stop("Invalid standardization factor")
    }
    selected <- merge(
        selected,
        distribution[, c("cohort", cell_column, "adjustment"), with = FALSE],
        by = c("cohort", cell_column),
        sort = FALSE
    )
    selected[, standardized_weight := base_weight * adjustment]
    selected
}

# Includes an in-group constant-reference Brier skill for interpretation.
# The reference uses the original historical training prevalence, not 2025 labels.
score_groups <- function(data, weight_column, scenario, historical_prevalence) {
    results <- lapply(primary_groups, function(group) {
        subset <- data[cohort == group & valid_weight(get(weight_column))]
        if (!nrow(subset)) {
            stop("Empty subgroup for ", scenario, ": ", group)
        }
        weights <- subset[[weight_column]]
        metrics <- weighted_metrics(
            subset$FMD,
            subset$selected_probability,
            weights
        )
        reference <- weighted_metrics(
            subset$FMD,
            rep(historical_prevalence, nrow(subset)),
            weights
        )
        data.frame(
            scenario = scenario,
            cohort = group,
            metrics,
            brier_skill_vs_historical = 1 - metrics$brier / reference$brier
        )
    })
    data.table::rbindlist(results)
}

# Difference convention is always AI/AN minus other single-race.
gap_from_metrics <- function(metrics, measure) {
    ai_value <- metrics[cohort == primary_groups[1]][[measure]][1]
    other_value <- metrics[cohort == primary_groups[2]][[measure]][1]
    ai_value - other_value
}
```
